idiom_name: dirty HashMap + tokio interval flush task over sqlx transactions
implementation_notes: Neither sqlx nor diesel provides a persistence context, so Rust makes you own the accumulator: a HashMap keyed by identity (coalescing by construction) drained by an async task that wakes on tokio::time::interval or a batch-size trigger and executes the batch through sqlx's Transaction, where commit() is explicit. The borrow checker forces explicit ownership of staged rows, which removes the accidental-sharing bugs the classic pattern invites; what replaces the classic structure is only the async runtime's timer and channels, so the roles remain hand-written. Honestly justified when write throughput matters; otherwise write through per change.
pitfalls: Never hold a std::sync::Mutex guard across .await: either keep the map lock-free between awaits or use tokio::sync::Mutex deliberately.
A panic in the flush task stops every write silently unless the task is supervised and restarted.
Staging the final value, not a delta, keeps coalescing bounded: appending every change to a Vec per key grows without limit under pressure.
